appearance_facts.fact: Orange slice labeled 'Apple (60 %)' occupies the largest angular extent, spanning roughly from the 12 o'clock position counter-clockwise to about the 10 o'clock position.
Dark red slice labeled 'Xiaomi (10 %)' is the smallest named brand slice, spanning roughly from 12 o'clock clockwise to about 4 o'clock.
Orange-red slice labeled 'Samsung (12 %)' spans roughly from 4 o'clock clockwise to about 7 o'clock.
Pale yellow slice labeled 'Others (18 %)' spans roughly from 7 o'clock counter-clockwise to about 10 o'clock.
Each slice contains a white text label with the brand name and a percentage in parentheses, positioned near the centroid of its slice.

printed_facts.fact: Title text: 'Smartphone Market Share in Europe'

public_definitions: User goal: 'Review the Europe smartphone market-share dashboard, then assign the next premium retail promotion to the brand with the highest current market_share.'
Policy table 'Premium promotion rule': 'Select the brand with the highest current market_share'; Decision metric: 'market_share'; Review scope: 'Europe smartphone brands'.
Form instruction: 'Use the dashboard market_share values as the evidence source; the next premium retail promotion is reserved for the current European market leader.'
Primary field: 'Premium retail promotion brand' with options 'Select Apple', 'Select Xiaomi', 'Select Samsung'.
uncertain: The dashboard percentages (60 + 10 + 12 + 18 = 100) are internally consistent, but the absolute market-share figures appear unusually high for real-world European smartphone data; this is taken at face value as the printed evidence.
'Others (18 %)' is not a selectable brand option, so it is excluded from the promotion assignment per the option list.
